old: the mind makes everything; everything is made of the mind. If you speak or act with a corrupted
new: the mind is chief of all; everything is made of the mind. If you speak or act with a corrupted
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); manoseṭṭhā = mind is chief; 'makes everything' is not in the text. Müller's opening cadence kept as recorded in the edition's divergences (update that note's wording).

old: the mind makes everything; everything is made of the mind. If you speak or act with a clear
new: the mind is chief of all; everything is made of the mind. If you speak or act with a clear
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); manoseṭṭhā = mind is chief; 'makes everything' is not in the text. Müller's opening cadence kept as recorded in the edition's divergences (update that note's wording).

old: he struck me, he beat me, he robbed me"—in those who hold on
new: he struck me, he got the better of me, he robbed me"—in those who hold on
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); akkocchi avadhi ajini ahāsi: abused, struck, defeated, robbed; Müller 'defeated'. 'Beat' after 'struck' loses the defeat.

old: he struck me, he beat me, he robbed me"—in those who let go
new: he struck me, he got the better of me, he robbed me"—in those who let go
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); akkocchi avadhi ajini ahāsi: abused, struck, defeated, robbed; Müller 'defeated'. 'Beat' after 'struck' loses the defeat.

old: Mara, the tempter, will overthrow
new: Mara will overthrow
why: Gloss policy: Pali taṃ ve pasahati māro; 'the tempter' is added. Mara is in the glossary.

old: they wander after empty desires.
new: they wander after wrong intentions.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); micchāsaṅkappagocarā, ranging in wrong intention; mirrors v12.

old: they follow desires that are real.
new: they follow right intentions.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); sammāsaṅkappagocarā, ranging in right intention; 'desires that are real' reads oddly.

old: give themselves over to carelessness
new: give themselves over to heedlessness
why: Term policy: pamāda = heedlessness throughout (v21 and v29 already); Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled).

old: Do not give yourself to carelessness; do not give yourself to the pleasures of desire.
new: Do not give yourself to heedlessness; do not give yourself to sensual delight.
why: Term policy (pamāda = heedlessness); Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); kāmarati = delight in sensual pleasure, Müller 'love and lust'.

old: drive out carelessness by heedfulness
new: drive out heedlessness by heedfulness
why: Term policy: pamāda = heedlessness; Pali pamādaṃ appamādena nudati.

old: like a swift horse leaving a slow one in its dust.
new: like a swift horse that leaves a weak one behind.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); sīghasso abalassaṃ hitvā: a swift horse leaving a weak one; 'in its dust' is an added stock idiom.

old: By heedfulness Indra rose to be lord of the gods. Heedfulness is forever praised; carelessness is forever blamed.
new: By heedfulness Maghavan rose to be lord of the gods. Heedfulness is forever praised; heedlessness is forever blamed.
why: Term policy (pamāda = heedlessness). Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); the text names Maghavā; 'Indra' is Müller's parenthetical gloss. Proper noun kept without a gloss (gloss policy).

old: dreads carelessness moves like a fire
new: dreads heedlessness moves like a fire
why: Term policy: pamāda = heedlessness; Pali pamāde bhayadassī.

old: dreads carelessness cannot fall back
new: dreads heedlessness cannot fall back
why: Term policy: pamāda = heedlessness.

old: he stands close upon Nirvana.
new: he is close to Nirvana.
why: 'Close upon' is dated (same fix as v372); Pali nibbānasseva santike.

old: Who will master this earth, and the realm of Death,
new: Who will master this earth, and the realm of Yama,
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); yamalokaṃ, Yama's world; Müller keeps Yama. Proper noun restored without a gloss (gloss policy); downgraded from medium, meaning was not wrong.

old: in training will master this earth, and the realm of Death,
new: in training will master this earth, and the realm of Yama,
why: Same as v44.

old: his mind elsewhere, as a flood
new: his mind caught up in them, as a flood
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); byāsattamanasaṃ, mind clinging/entangled, not absent.

old: his mind elsewhere, before he
new: his mind caught up in them, before he
why: Same as v47.

old: are the fine words of one who speaks well but does not act.
new: are fine words that bear no fruit in one who does not act on them.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); v51 subhāsitā vācā aphalā hoti akubbato: fine words are fruitless in one who does not act; restores the 51/52 mirror.

old: are the fine words of one who speaks well and acts on them, and they bear fruit.
new: are fine words that bear fruit in one who acts on them.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); v52 saphalā hoti kubbato; mirrors v51.

old: A good person reaches every quarter.
new: The fragrance of the good spreads in every direction.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); sabbā disā sappuriso pavāyati: the good person's scent blows in every direction; keeps the verse's image.

old: whose fruit he receives gladly and with a glad heart.
new: whose fruit he receives with delight and a happy heart.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); haṭṭho sumano: delighted, happy-minded; 'gladly ... glad' doubles one word.

old: Let the fool crave a reputation he has not earned,
new: The fool wants a reputation he has not earned,
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); asantaṃ bhāvanam iccheyya describes the fool's wish; Müller's archaic 'Let the fool wish' now reads as permission.

old: crave a son, or wealth, or power,
new: crave a son, or wealth, or a kingdom,
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); na puttam icche na dhanaṃ na raṭṭhaṃ; raṭṭha = kingdom, Müller 'lordship'.

old: their aim is emptiness, the freedom that depends on nothing—Nirvana.
new: they range in the freedom that is empty and without sign.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); suññato animitto ca vimokkho yassa gocaro: empty and signless liberation is their range, not aim; 'depends on nothing' misreads animitta; 'Nirvana' is Müller's parenthetical (gloss policy).

old: whose aim is emptiness, the freedom that depends on nothing—Nirvana—his track
new: whose range is the freedom that is empty and without sign, his track
why: Same as v92.

old: Such a one bears all things
new: Such a one, true to his vows, bears all things
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); subbato, 'of good vows' (Müller 'who does his duty') was dropped.

old: not even Brahman could
new: not even Brahma could
why: Müller-error policy: Pali saha Brahmunā names the god Brahmā; 'Brahman' now means the impersonal absolute.

old: 127. Not in the sky, not in the middle of the sea, not deep in a mountain cave—nowhere in all the world is there a place where you can escape your own evil deed.
new: 127, 128. Not in the sky, not in the middle of the sea, not deep in a mountain cave—nowhere in all the world is there a place where you can escape your own evil deed. Not in the sky, not in the middle of the sea, not deep in a mountain cave—nowhere in all the world is there a place where death cannot overtake you.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); v128 na antalikkhe ... yatthaṭṭhitaṃ nappasaheyya maccu (no place where death would not overpower one) was missing; Chapter X opens at 129. Restored inside the chapter's last segment with the edition's own joint-number form ('153, 154.'); no segment added. Bundled Müller prints the death verse as 127 and has no 128.

old: and blow will fall on blow.
new: and the rod will come back on you.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); paṭidaṇḍā phuseyyu taṃ: retaliation would touch you; keeps the chapter's 'rod' (daṇḍa).

old: then you have come close to Nirvana,
new: then you have reached Nirvana,
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); esa patto'si nibbānaṃ, you have reached Nirvana; Müller 'thou hast reached Nirvana'.

old: who has not gone beyond his cravings.
new: who has not gone beyond doubt.
why: Müller-error policy: Pali avitiṇṇakaṅkhaṃ, one who has not crossed doubt; Müller's 'desires' is a mistranslation.

old: be eager and alive.
new: be ardent and full of urgency.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); ātāpino saṃvegino: ardent, stirred to urgency.

old: sickly, full of cravings,
new: sickly, full of many thoughts,
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); bahusaṅkappaṃ, full of many thoughts (Müller same).

old: so the good pass it on, one to another.
new: so the good teach it to the good.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); santo have sabbhi pavedayanti: the good declare it to the good; 'pass it on' suggests virtue is handed down.

old: My mind has reached the unmade, the unconditioned, Nirvana;
new: My mind has reached the unconditioned;
why: Gloss policy: Pali visaṅkhāragataṃ cittaṃ is one term; 'Nirvana' is Müller's parenthetical.

old: Do for yourself what you would have others do; train yourself before you train anyone else, for the self is the hardest of all to master. Only the well-mastered are fit to master others.
new: Do yourself what you teach others to do. Master yourself first, and you may master others; for the self is the hardest of all to master.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); attānañce tathā kayirā yathāññam anusāsati; sudanto vata dametha, attā hi kira duddamo. The old wording echoes the Golden Rule and says the second clause twice.

old: like the reed that dies the year it flowers.
new: like the reed whose fruiting is its own death.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); phalāni kaṭṭhakasseva attaghātāya phallati; give the image, not an explanation of the plant.

old: Follow the path of virtue. The virtuous rest in peace,
new: Follow the path of virtue. The virtuous live at ease,
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); dhammacārī sukhaṃ seti, lives/sleeps happily; 'rest in peace' is the epitaph formula.

old: not the way of wrongdoing. The virtuous rest in peace,
new: not the way of wrongdoing. The virtuous live at ease,
why: Same as v168.

old: and hardest of all, rare beyond rare, is the arising of a Buddha,
new: and hard is the arising of a Buddha,
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); kiccho buddhānaṃ uppādo is the fourth of four parallel 'hard' clauses, unranked.

old: the one who wounds another is no true seeker.
new: the one who wounds another is no true ascetic.
why: Term policy: samaṇa = ascetic; 'seeker' carries a modern spiritual sense.

old: in the Buddha, in the Dhamma—the Law—and in the Sangha—the Order—and who sees
new: in the Buddha, in the teaching, and in the Order, and who sees
why: Gloss and term policy: one name each (dhamma = the teaching, saṅgha = the Order); the dashed glosses break the refuge formula.

old: happy is the teaching of the true Law;
new: happy is the proclaiming of the true teaching;
why: Term policy: dhamma = the teaching; Pali saddhammadesanā.

old: all grief and longing;
new: all grief and lament;
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); tiṇṇasokapariddave: pariddava = lamentation.

old: grieves a long road;
new: grieves for a long time;
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); dīghaddhānaṃ socati, grieves a long while; 'grieves a long road' is not English.

old: a longing for the Ineffable, Nirvana, has awakened
new: a longing for the Ineffable has awakened
why: Gloss policy: Pali anakkhāta stands alone; 'Nirvana' is Müller's parenthetical.

old: go to the unchanging place, Nirvana, and
new: go to the unchanging place, and
why: Gloss policy: Pali accutaṃ ṭhānaṃ; 'Nirvana' is Müller's parenthetical.

old: But the one whom the discerning praise day after day—flawless, wise, rich in understanding and in virtue—who would dare to blame, worthy as a coin of the purest river-gold? Even the gods praise such a one; even Brahman praises him.
new: But who would dare to blame the one whom the discerning praise day after day—flawless, wise, rich in understanding and in virtue, like a coin of gold from the Jambu river? Even the gods praise such a one; even Brahma praises him.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); nikkhaṃ jambonadasseva ko taṃ ninditum arahati ... brahmunāpi pasaṃsito. The question lacked an object, the river's name was dropped, and Brahmā was 'Brahman' (Müller-error policy).

old: Scriptures decay when they go unrecited; houses decay when they go unrepaired; beauty decays through sloth; a watchman decays through carelessness.
new: Scripture is tainted when it goes unrecited, a house when it goes unrepaired; sloth is the taint of beauty, and heedlessness the taint of a watchman.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); asajjhāyamalā mantā, anuṭṭhānamalā gharā, malaṃ vaṇṇassa kosajjaṃ, pamādo rakkhato malaṃ: 241-243 are one chain on mala (taint); pamāda = heedlessness (term policy).

old: outward acts do not make a holy man. People delight in what holds them back, but the Tathagatas, the Buddhas, are free
new: there is no true ascetic outside this teaching. People delight in what holds them back, but the Tathagatas are free
why: Müller-error policy: Pali samaṇo natthi bāhire, no ascetic outside (this teaching); 'outward acts' is Müller's reading. 'the Buddhas' is his parenthetical (gloss policy).

old: outward acts do not make a holy man. Nothing made
new: there is no true ascetic outside this teaching. Nothing made
why: Same as v254.

old: not by force but fairly, by what is right, who is guided by what is right and is discerning—that one is called just, established in dhamma.
new: not by force but fairly and by law, who is guarded by the law and discerning—that one is called just, one who stands in the law.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); dhammena samena neti pare, dhammassa gutto medhāvī, dhammaṭṭho: 'by what is right' came twice and 'dhamma' was left untranslated (term policy: law where dhamma means justice).

old: and of all who have eyes, the one who truly sees—the Buddha.
new: and of all beings on two feet, the one who has eyes to see.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); dipadānañca cakkhumā: of two-footed beings, the one with eyes; 'the Buddha' is an added gloss.

old: you will bewilder Mara, the tempter.
new: you will bewilder Mara.
why: Gloss policy: Pali mārass' etaṃ pamohanaṃ.

old: to draw out the arrow of craving.
new: to draw out the arrow.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); sallakantanaṃ, the removal of the arrow; 'of craving' is a gloss.

old: "All conditioned things are impermanent" (sabbe sankhara anicca)—
new: "All conditioned things are impermanent"—
why: Parenthesis policy: Pali transliteration is apparatus, not text.

old: "All conditioned things are suffering" (sabbe sankhara dukkha)—
new: "All conditioned things are suffering"—
why: Parenthesis policy.

old: "All things are without a self" (sabbe dhamma anatta)—
new: "All things are without a self"—
why: Parenthesis policy.

old: Tend the road of peace—the Nirvana the Buddha has shown.
new: Tend the road to peace, to Nirvana, which the Buddha has shown.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); santimaggam eva brūhaya, nibbānaṃ sugatena desitaṃ (Nirvana is in the Pali); 'the Nirvana' stumbles.

old: his mind on other things
new: his mind caught up in them
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); byāsattamanasaṃ, as in v47-48 (kept consistent).

old: two learned kings, and having destroyed a kingdom along with its tiger,
new: two learned kings, and a tiger as the fifth,
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); veyagghapañcamaṃ hantvā: with a tiger as the fifth; v295 has no kingdom, carried over from v294.

old: set on the community.
new: set on the Order.
why: Term policy: saṅgha = the Order (as v190, v194).

old: hard it is to enjoy the world. Hard is life in the monastery, and painful is life in a house;
new: hard it is to delight in that life. Hard and painful is life in a household;
why: Müller-error policy: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); duppabbajjaṃ durabhiramaṃ, durāvāsā gharā dukkhā: going forth is hard, delighting in it is hard, the household is hard and painful; 'monastery' is Müller's.

old: Many a man whose shoulders are wrapped in the yellow robe is undisciplined
new: Many who wear the yellow robe around their shoulders are undisciplined
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); kāsāvakaṇṭhā bahavo (many); fixes the shift from 'many a man ... is' to 'their'.

old: reach the untrodden country, Nirvana.
new: reach the untrodden country.
why: Gloss policy: Pali agataṃ disaṃ; 'Nirvana' is Müller's parenthetical.

old: his temples streaming in must and hard to hold,
new: in rut, his temples streaming, and hard to hold,
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); kaṭukabhedano, the rutting discharge; 'must' reads as the verb.

old: Take heed; guard your own mind.
new: Delight in heedfulness; guard your own mind.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); appamādaratā hotha; restores the work's keyword.

old: To be a good mother in this world is a joy, and to be a good father is a joy; to live as one who has gone forth is a joy, and to live as a holy one is a joy.
new: To honor your mother is a joy in this world, and to honor your father is a joy; to honor ascetics is a joy, and to honor Brahmins is a joy.
why: Müller-error policy: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); matteyyatā, petteyyatā, sāmaññatā, brahmaññatā = reverence toward mother, father, ascetics, brahmins; Müller's 'the state of a mother' misled the edition.

old: so that Mara, the tempter, may not
new: so that Mara may not
why: Gloss policy: Pali mā vo naḷaṃva sotova māro bhañji punappunaṃ.

old: So let the seeker drive out craving
new: So let the monk drive out craving
why: Term policy: bhikkhu = monk.

old: The gift of the Dhamma surpasses all gifts; the taste of the Dhamma surpasses all tastes; the delight in the Dhamma surpasses
new: The gift of the teaching surpasses all gifts; the taste of the teaching surpasses all tastes; the delight in the teaching surpasses
why: Term policy: dhamma = the teaching.

old: Though a monk receive but little,
new: Though a monk receives little,
why: Archaic subjunctive.

old: loving-kindness, who has faith in the teaching of the Buddha, will reach the place of peace — Nirvana — where
new: loving-kindness, who has faith in the teaching of the Buddha, will reach the place of peace, where
why: Gloss policy: Pali padaṃ santaṃ; 'Nirvana' is Müller's parenthetical. Apply before the dash pass.

old: and do not be careless.
new: and do not be heedless.
why: Term policy: Pali mā ca pamādo.

old: Be careless, and you may
new: Be heedless, and you may
why: Term policy: Pali mā lohaguḷaṃ gilī pamatto.

old: stands close upon Nirvana.
new: is close to Nirvana.
why: 'Close upon' is dated; Pali nibbānasantike.

old: full of gladness, who has faith in the teaching of the Buddha, will reach the place of peace — Nirvana — where
new: full of gladness, who has faith in the teaching of the Buddha, will reach the place of peace, where
why: Same as v368.

old: you will know the Uncreated, Nirvana.
new: you will know the Uncreated.
why: Gloss policy: Pali akataññū; 'Nirvana' added.

old: crossed to the far shore of both teachings—restraint and meditation—then
new: crossed to the far shore in both states, then
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); dvayesu dhammesu, 'in two states' (traditionally calm and insight); the dashed gloss is not in the text.

old: wears cast-off rags, worn thin to the bone,
new: wears cast-off rags, lean, his veins standing out,
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); kisaṃ dhamanisanthataṃ describes the man, not the rags.

old: he is only a man who says "sir" to himself.
new: he is a Brahmin in name only, one who says "sir" to others.
why: Pali from the verifier's own knowledge (not bundled); bhovādī nāma so hoti: one who addresses others as 'bho', a Brahmin by name; 'says sir to himself' is not in the text.
